Electrochemical ODI-[5+2] Cascade for the Syntheses of Diversely
Functionalized Bicyclo[3.2.1]octane Frameworks
Zhaobo Liu, Jialei Hu, * and Hanfeng Ding *
Cite This: Org. Lett. 2021, 23, 6745 −6749 Read Online
ACCESS Metrics & More Article Recommendations *sı Supporting Information
ABSTRACT: A metal- and hypervalent iodine reagent-free electro-
chemical oxidative dearomatization-induced [5+2] cycloaddition/pinacol
rearrangement cascade reaction was described. The electrosynthetic
method showed strong tolerance for vinylphenols, ethynylphenols, and
allenylphenols, which thus enabled the rapid assembly of diversely
functionalized bicyclo[3.2.1]octanes in 41 −95% yields and up to >20:1
dr. This protocol could be scaled up to gram amounts and should ﬁnd
wide application in complex natural product synthesis.
B
icyclo[3.2.1]octane is a structurally ubiquitous motif
found in various families of biologically active natural
products, as represented by terpenoids and alkaloids ( Scheme
1a). Due to its indispensable branching-point position leading
to the other fused-ring systems, including bicyclo[2.2.2]-,
bicyclo[3.3.0]-, and tricyclo[3.2.1.0]octanes, in the biogenetic
pathway of tetracyclic diterpenoids and its structure-related
prominent bioactivities,
1 the bicyclo[3.2.1]octane sca ﬀold has
made itself the subject of intense research and evoked
continuing synthetic innovation. To date, numerous elegant
methodologies have been disclosed with respect to its
construction,2 which can be chie ﬂy categorized into single-
bond cyclizations, 3 multiple-bond cyclizations, 4 and ring-
reorganization reactions. 5 Recently, we have described a
novel and e ﬃcient oxidative dearomatization-induced (ODI)
[5+2] cycloaddition 6/pinacol rearrangement cascade reaction
with the aid of a hypervalent iodine(III) reagent, which o ﬀers a
robust synthetic protocol for the assembly of bicyclo[3.2.1]-
octane frameworks from readily available vinylphenols
(Scheme 1c).7 Subsequently, substantial progress in tetracyclic
diterpenoid syntheses via ODI-[5+2] cascade reaction has
been achieved through our persistent e ﬀorts in the past few
years.
7a,8 Nevertheless, during the adventures, we found that
the non-negligible drawbacks associated with the strongly
acidic byproducts derived from the hypervalent iodine reagents
greatly limited functional group tolerance, especially for the
acid sensitive benzyl alcohol-containing substrates due to the
tendency to generate an unstable quinonmethide intermedia-
te.
7a,8c Therefore, further improvements remain urgently
needed in terms of the compatibility between diverse
functional groups and the established conditions for the
ODI-[5+2] cascade reactions.
Organic electrosynthesis has proven to be a practical
technique for the development of novel chemical trans-
formations driven by redox processes with electric current. 9
An obvious advantage of employing the electrochemical
methods is that such reactions can be triggered by precise
manipulation of the electri c current or potential, thus
permitting chemists to obtain products that are chemical
reagent-based synthetically inaccessible or low-e ﬃcient.
10 In
1991, the Yamamura group described an interesting anodic
oxidation of vinylphenol ( Scheme 1b).
11a Upon treatment of 1
with a constant current to initiate a two-electron oxidative
dearomatization, phenoxy cation 2 was generated in situ, which
then reacted with the tethered ole ﬁni nam a n n e ro f
intramolecular [5+2] cycloaddition. The reaction ﬁnally
delivered tricycle 3 in 59% yield. On the basis of this key
transformation, total syntheses of several cedrene-type natural
products were accomplished.
11b However, despite the
appealing application potential, the substrate scope of this
protocol had not been fully demonstrated. Inspired by the
seminal work described above, we herein report an electro-
chemical ODI-[5+2] cycloaddition/pinacol rearrangement
cascade reaction of various types of phenol substrates,
including vinylphenols, ethynylphenols, and allenylphenols
(Scheme 1 c), which exhibited evident advantages over
conventional hypervalent iodine oxidation.
We ﬁrst identi ﬁed the optimal reaction conditions for the
electrochemical ODI-[5+2] cascade by employing vinylphenol
4a as a model substrate ( Table 1 ; for a detailed optimization,
see Table S1 ), which involve the constant-current (5 mA)
electrolysis using a graphite anode and a graphite cathode in an
undivided cell containing an electrolyte solution of n-Bu

(0.1 M) in MeCN, and o-nitrophenol (3 equiv) as the additive.
Under these conditions, the desired bicyclo[3.2.1]octane 5a
was isolated in 90% yield (entry 1, Table 1 ). Subsequently,
switching the solvent to DCE, HFIP, or MeOH resulted in a
signiﬁcantly decreased yield (entries 2 −4). Other electrolytes
such as n-Bu4NPF6 could also be used without a ﬀecting the
yield or current e ﬃciency (entry 5). A relatively suitable
current density was potentially important, because a lower or
higher current (2 or 10 mA, respectively) showed a negative
inﬂuence on the cascade reaction (entries 6 and 7). Because of
the generation of benzoquinone byproducts, a reduced
eﬃciency was observed when the reaction mixture was
exposed to moisture (entry 8). As a comparison, the
replacement of an acid additive under anhydrous conditions
has tri ﬂing impacts on the yield (entry 9). Attempts to reduce
the amount of additive led to a diminished yield and
conversion (entry 10). Furthermore, the reaction could be
achieved on a gram scale without a decrease in yield, albeit
requiring a prolonged reaction time (entry 11). On the other
hand, vinylphenols bearing an ethoxy group or a benzyloxy
group instead of the methoxy group were also compatible and
provided an equal e ﬃciency, whereas a rapid decomposition of
the corresponding catechol-type substrate was observed.
Having secured the optimal conditions, we next evaluated
the scope of the anodic ODI-[5+2] cascade reaction using an
array of vinylphenols with di ﬀerent electronic and steric
variations (Scheme 2). The electrochemical protocol proved to
be suitable for a wide range of substituents, including alkyl,
phenyl, halogens, and esters at various positions of the phenol
ring, leading to the corresponding products in good to
excellent yields (63 −94%, 5b−j and 5t). These results
indicated that the electronic e ﬀects and steric hindrance of
the phenol motif had little in ﬂuence on this reaction. The side
chain of the vinylphenol showed a strong tolerance to
substituents of broad types, such as methyl ( 4m, 4n, and
4q), hydroxyl ( 4k and 4o), methoxy ( 4l), and gem-diester
(4p), again resulting in high e ﬃciency and excellent
diastereoselectivities (84 −96%, >10:1 dr). These outcomes
presumably arose from minimization of steric interactions
between the substituents on the side chain and the carbonyl
group in an exo-transition state ( 6a vs 6b). It is worth
emphasizing that one major advantage of our method lies in
the e ﬃcient transformation of the benzylic alcohol-containing
substrates in an almost neutral reaction environment, which
were previously found to a ﬀord the anticipated products in the
presence of hypervalent iodine reagents in signi ﬁcantly
decreased yields owing to the tendency to generate the
unstable quinone methides ( 4k and 4l). Notably, 1,1- and 1,2-
disubstituted terminal alkenes were also viable substrates,
providing the desired products with satisfactory yields (81%
and 86% for 5r and 5s, respectively). Compared with 5a,
cyclohexyl-fused 5u was delivered with reduced e
ﬃciency
(45%). The outcome described above was probably attributed
to the lack of the Thorpe −Ingold eﬀect12 in the cycloaddition
step. To our delight, 5v, an advanced intermediate en route to
rhodomollanol A, was also achieved from 4v in 71% yield
under the standard conditions. It should be mentioned that the
latter was extremely acid-labile. Therefore, a THP prepro-
tection of its benzyl alcohol and addition of an extraneous base
to the reaction mixture were required in a previous hypervalent
iodine oxidation.
8c Moreover, 4w could be transformed into
5w, a key intermediate of stemarin, in a much improved yield
(84%), as well. 8b These examples clearly implied the future
synthetic application prospects of this established protocol.

generating bicyclo[3.2.1]octane products that embedded with

substrates ( Scheme 3 ). In its present form, the scope of the
reaction encompassed ethynylphenols with variable steric
substitutions on the phenol ring ( 7a−f and 7o), di ﬀerent
functionalities on the side chain ( 7g−j), and skipped enynes
(7k) and even internal alkynes ( 7l−n). Accordingly, the
expected products were obtained in good to excellent yields
(70−95%, 8a−o). Among these experiments, an unexpected
double-bond migration was detected with respect to 7k, which
was transformed into a thermodynamically more stable
dienone 8k. Furthermore, in contrast to vinylphenols, we
were surprised to ﬁnd that the substrates bearing electron-
withdrawing groups (Cl, Br, CO
2Me, etc.) on the phenol ring
(7p−s) exclusively a ﬀorded the Diels −Alder adducts (72 −
80%, 8p−s), which was probably due to the demethylation to
generate an unmasked o-benzoquinone prior to [5+2]
cycloaddition.8d
Encouraged by the aforementioned promising results, we
further extended the scope of the reaction to allenylphenols,
which appear to be more vulnerable under hypervalent iodine
oxidation ( Scheme 4 ). Fortunately, the mild electrochemical
conditions successfully overcame the highly acid sensitive
nature of these compounds. Greatly improved yields for the
formation of 10a−p were realized when compared with those
of conventional chemical oxidation. By employing the well-
designed electrolytic method, allenylphenols containing both
electron neutral and de ﬁcient phenol rings could be e ﬃciently
and regioselectively conve rted into the corresponding
bicyclo[3.2.1]octanes beari ng an exocyclic double bond
adjacent to the carbonyl moiety (71 −92%, 10a−k). Gratify-
ingly, substrates bearing distinct substitutions on the side chain

products in good to excellent yields and satisfactory dr values
(41−90%, >4.6:1 dr, 10l−p).
In conclusion, we have developed a mild electrochemical
ODI-[5+2] cycloaddition/pinacol rearrangement cascade
reaction. Compared with hypervalent iodine(III)-mediated
oxidative conditions, this new protocol signi ﬁcantly improves
the reaction e ﬃciency and substrate compatibility, hence
providing rapid access to di versely functionalized
bicyclo[3.2.1]octanes with good to excellent yields and
diastereoselectivities. Its synthetic value has been preliminarily
demonstrated by gram-scale preparations of the core frame-
works and successful application in the construction of several
key intermediates en route to complex natural products.
Further studies of application of this methodology are
currently underway in our laboratory.
